Check: Confirm the endpoint is expected to be online and managed
Evidence to capture: Customer; site; hostname; durable device ID; owner; expected operating hours
Likely cause: Planned shutdown; sleep; retirement; stale inventory
Safe next action: Verify business context before changing the endpoint
Escalation trigger: Device is production-critical or status cannot be confirmed

Check: Record the platform device ID and last successful heartbeat
Evidence to capture: Device URL or ID; last check-in; last inventory; last job result; platform time zone
Likely cause: Stale console data; delayed ingestion; wrong record
Safe next action: Preserve the original platform evidence
Escalation trigger: Multiple records disagree or the last-known state is missing

Check: Determine whether one device or a shared cohort is affected
Evidence to capture: Affected count; customer; site; OS; agent version; network; policy; first observed time
Likely cause: Shared outage; policy change; certificate issue; network block
Safe next action: Group by common attributes before per-device repair
Escalation trigger: More than one customer or site is affected

Check: Check approved alternate access and business risk
Evidence to capture: Alternate access method; workload criticality; backup state; maintenance window
Likely cause: No safe access path; high-impact workload
Safe next action: Define authority; stop conditions; rollback; communication
Escalation trigger: No approved access or change window exists

Check: Confirm power; boot; sleep; and network state from an independent source
Evidence to capture: Uptime; console or hypervisor state; DHCP or switch evidence; user confirmation
Likely cause: Powered off; sleeping; boot failure; network isolation
Safe next action: Restore the underlying endpoint state first
Escalation trigger: Boot failure; encryption recovery; or suspected isolation

Check: Verify the agent package and service are present
Evidence to capture: Installed package; service name; startup type; binary path; version; signature
Likely cause: Agent removed; incomplete update; damaged install
Safe next action: Use vendor-supported detection and repair steps
Escalation trigger: Unexpected binary; signature failure; or unauthorized removal

Check: Capture service and process state before restarting
Evidence to capture: Service state; exit code; process ID; crash data; recent start attempts
Likely cause: Stopped service; dependency failure; crash loop
Safe next action: Preserve evidence; then perform one authorized restart
Escalation trigger: Repeated crash; service tampering; or security detection

Check: Collect agent and operating-system logs for the failure window
Evidence to capture: Agent log excerpt; event logs; timestamps; error codes; time zone
Likely cause: Authentication; TLS; proxy; update; resource; or dependency failure
Safe next action: Correlate the first failure with a documented cause
Escalation trigger: Logs are missing; altered; or show suspicious privileged activity

Check: Verify DNS and route to the exact vendor endpoints
Evidence to capture: Resolved addresses; route; proxy path; vendor status page; observation time
Likely cause: DNS failure; proxy error; route outage; platform incident
Safe next action: Correct the narrow verified dependency
Escalation trigger: Broad outage or vendor service incident

Check: Test outbound ports and TLS without weakening controls
Evidence to capture: Destination; port; TLS result; certificate chain; inspection behavior
Likely cause: Firewall block; TLS inspection; expired certificate; clock skew
Safe next action: Apply the narrow documented network change and retest
Escalation trigger: Certificate trust issue; unknown destination; or global bypass proposed

Check: Check proxy; content filter; EDR; and application-control events
Evidence to capture: Proxy logs; block event; detection name; signer; hash; policy owner
Likely cause: Security control blocked or quarantined the agent
Safe next action: Validate vendor artifacts and use a scoped time-bounded exception only if approved
Escalation trigger: Malware suspicion; unsigned artifact; or fleet-wide block

Check: Verify endpoint time synchronization and certificate validity
Evidence to capture: Local time; time source; drift; certificate dates; chain status
Likely cause: Clock drift; expired certificate; trust-store problem
Safe next action: Restore trusted time or certificate state through the approved path
Escalation trigger: Certificate replacement or trust change is required

Check: Confirm the agent is enrolled in the intended tenant and site
Evidence to capture: Local enrollment ID; platform tenant; site; device ID; install token record
Likely cause: Wrong tenant; stale token; duplicate enrollment
Safe next action: Stop automation and reconcile identity before re-enrollment
Escalation trigger: Cross-customer placement or tenant ambiguity

Check: Search for duplicate; renamed; retired; or replacement records
Evidence to capture: Hostname; serial; hardware ID; agent ID; record history; last seen
Likely cause: Duplicate object; renamed device; reimage; stale record
Safe next action: Choose one authoritative identity and preserve history
Escalation trigger: Two active privileged records or conflicting customer ownership

Check: Check whether credentials; tokens; or certificates were rotated or revoked
Evidence to capture: Rotation event; token age; certificate thumbprint; revocation time; change ticket
Likely cause: Expired or revoked enrollment material
Safe next action: Use the vendor-supported renewal or repair workflow
Escalation trigger: Unexplained revocation or possible credential exposure

Check: Separate heartbeat failure from a stale module or job
Evidence to capture: Fresh heartbeat; inventory time; patch scan; script result; remote-session state
Likely cause: Single module failure; queue delay; stale cached status
Safe next action: Repair the affected function rather than reinstalling the whole agent
Escalation trigger: Privileged functions disagree about device identity or state

Check: Define success; stop; rollback; and evidence before repair
Evidence to capture: Expected heartbeat time; functions to test; rollback trigger; approver
Likely cause: Unbounded troubleshooting; unclear acceptance
Safe next action: Write the bounded repair plan before execution
Escalation trigger: No rollback path for a production-critical endpoint

Check: Fix the verified dependency before restarting or reinstalling
Evidence to capture: Cause; change; actor; command or policy; start and end time; output
Likely cause: Network; service; certificate; policy; resource; or platform dependency
Safe next action: Make the least-disruptive approved change
Escalation trigger: Cause remains unknown or change requires broad exclusions

Check: Prefer vendor-supported repair over immediate reinstall
Evidence to capture: Repair method; package version; result; preserved configuration and identity
Likely cause: Damaged agent files; failed update; recoverable configuration
Safe next action: Run supported repair on one representative endpoint
Escalation trigger: Repair changes identity or fails repeatedly

Check: If reinstalling; control tenant; site; duplicate-record; and uninstall evidence
Evidence to capture: Authorization; uninstall result; residual files or services; new enrollment ID; record mapping
Likely cause: Irrecoverable install; identity reset required
Safe next action: Reinstall one endpoint; reconcile old and new records before scaling
Escalation trigger: Duplicate active records; wrong tenant; or incomplete removal

Check: Confirm a fresh heartbeat and current inventory after repair
Evidence to capture: New check-in time; inventory timestamp; agent version; service state
Likely cause: Repair incomplete; ingestion delay; stale console
Safe next action: Wait the documented interval; then re-evaluate current evidence
Escalation trigger: Heartbeat remains absent after the supported recovery window

Check: Test monitoring; script; patch; and remote-support functions separately
Evidence to capture: Alert test; bounded script output; patch scan; remote-session audit event
Likely cause: Partial recovery; one module still stale
Safe next action: Open owned work for each failed function
Escalation trigger: Privileged function fails or produces no audit evidence

Check: Reconcile the affected cohort and every platform record
Evidence to capture: Recovered; offline; retired; duplicate; wrong tenant; unknown; exception counts
Likely cause: Hidden residual failures; incomplete fleet repair
Safe next action: Assign owner and due date to every unresolved endpoint
Escalation trigger: Unknown or cross-customer records remain

Check: Record cause; prevention; exception; and closure evidence
Evidence to capture: Root cause; corrective action; detection change; owner; review date; customer acceptance
Likely cause: Repeatable operational gap; weak monitoring; undocumented dependency
Safe next action: Update runbooks; alerts; maintenance process; and evidence retention
Escalation trigger: Residual risk lacks approval or expiry
